findings.title: checkout bypasses cart's public API to import cart's internal pricing module

evidence.quote:
import { Cart, total } from "../cart/cart";
import { priceOf } from "../cart/pricing";

findings.note: checkout imports cart's internal pricing.ts directly instead of only cart.ts's public total(). Legacy branch only prices the first item via priceOf, diverging from total(); no boundary tool constrains cart's internals (only eslint:recommended configured).

looks_bad_but_fine.why: stock.ts imports `type Cart` from cart.ts, which together with cart.ts -> pricing.ts -> stock.ts forms the cycle in the given lead. The stock->cart edge is a type-only import (`import type`), erased at compile time, so there is no runtime cycle; all three files also live in the same cart component, so per the traps this is a design smell internal to one cohesive package rather than a cross-module architecture cycle.

not_assessed: No claims about test coverage, CVEs, EOL/currency of dependencies, library-level deprecation status, test flakiness, or exploitability were made; the @deprecated tag in src/util/format-legacy.ts is an in-repo JSDoc annotation only, not an assessed library deprecation.
